newsitem.title: FRANCE: MEPs want EU-wide response to epidemics.
newsitem.headline: MEPs want EU-wide response to epidemics.

text.p: The European Parliament called on Wednesday for a central European agency to control the spread of diseases like tuberculosis and mad cow disease (BSE).

MEP's adopted a report by French Union for Europe MEP Christian Cabrol which says the member states' reaction to BSE and its human equivalent Creutzfeldt Jakob Disease (CJD) illustrates the need for an EU-wide early warning system and coordinated action to prevent epidemics.
"The general public can only view with alarm the disorderly and incoherent reactions which the (BSE-CJD) crisis has produced," the report said.
MEPs said European Commission plans to create a network of national monitoring agencies would not be enough to prevent the spread of contagious diseases and illnesses.
Some member states do not have national agencies.

So while one EU country might check all incomers from third countries where there are serious diseases like ebola (Zaire) or legionnaires' disease (the United States), contagious people can still cross the border from neighbouring EU states where no checks are made.

Even in those member states which do possess a national surveillance agency, the monitoring and disease control methods vary, so it is impossible to compare the data and combat the spread of epidemics effectively.
Some diseases are not monitored at all, according to Cabrol's report.

Cabrol, a doctor, argued that if the member states can see the logic of having a European centre for monitoring the spread of AIDS (set up in 1987), then they should adopt a similar approach to other communicable diseases.
The Commission had not suggested such an approach for fear EU health ministers would reject it, an official with the parliament's public health committee told Reuters recently.
Parliament approved the Commission's proposal for a network -- COM(96)78 -- as a first step, but introduced amendments to strengthen it.
As well as a central monitoring agency, they called for an early warning system for passing on to member state authorities details of emerging or recurring diseases.
Cabrol's report urged the Commission to state more clearly how it expects the surveillance network to be financed.
"If certain member states are unable to meet this financial obligation, the entire system will collapse," it warned.
